questions.question: Retries are enabled in production, which makes the backlog's queue-race item live rather than theoretical: when two jobs race, the loser exits 1, and the dashboard can't tell that from "this job is bad" — so it stops choosing a good job whose only fault was arriving second. The fix is a distinct exit code the dashboard treats as no evidence, mirroring a pattern that already exists. It shares this unit's maintenance window and test run. Include it?

options.label: Include it (Recommended)
options.description: Adds about an hour: a constant in the queue module, one exit path, a `declined` flag through the two callers, and tests with a negative control. Separate commit, so it rolls back independently. The alternative is paying the test run and the maintenance window twice.

options.label: Recovery only
options.description: Keep the diff to worker lifecycle. The queue race stays open; it bites only when two jobs actually collide, and the cost is one good job the dashboard refuses until someone retries it by hand.

questions.question: The supervisor will restart workers unattended. Should those restarts be recorded where the dashboard can show them?

options.label: Record and show in History (Recommended)
options.description: Append to a log file and merge into the History tab beside the other lifecycle events. That tab's stated job is "was the service up", and an unattended restart is exactly that. Costs a small dashboard change.

options.label: Journal only
options.description: Restarts go to the system journal via stdout and nowhere else. Cheaper and no dashboard change, but the only way to learn a worker restarted itself is to log in and look.

# Dashboard: offline mode and blocklists

## Context

The service has a control dashboard for **local** development only. It has never been reachable from outside the machine it runs on, which is why it has no authentication and why every action it exposes assumes a trusted operator is the one clicking.

This plan adds two things that need it to keep assuming that.

## 1. Offline mode

A switch that takes the service down for maintenance without stopping the process.
